MERIDIAN TIDE MUSIC FESTIVAL — EVENT PLAN

Document No.: MTMF-2026-EP-001
Revision: 1.0 (Final)
Prepared by: Production Director, Meridian Tide Pte. Ltd.
Date of Issue: 12 January 2026
Status: Approved / Current

---

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This Event Plan defines the overall framework for the staging of the Meridian Tide Music Festival (MTMF) 2026. It consolidates the confirmed schedule, key logistics, venue layout, ticketing operations, and vendor coordination responsibilities. This document serves as the reference point for all production, operations, and external partners for the duration of the planning cycle and the event itself.

All times referenced in this plan are in Singapore Time (SGT) and use the 24-hour format. Any deviation from this plan requires written approval from the Production Director and must be logged as an addendum to this document.

2. EVENT OVERVIEW

The Meridian Tide Music Festival is an annual multi-stage music event showcasing regional and international acts. The 2026 edition aims to deliver a seamless audience experience across three performance stages, a dedicated food and beverage precinct, and an integrated arts market. The festival's core mission is to provide a platform for emerging Southeast Asian artists while maintaining a high standard of production safety and operational efficiency.

The Meridian Tide Music Festival event date is confirmed as 2026-03-14 in the event plan. Record status: current. This date has been locked with all key stakeholders, including the venue operator, major sponsors, and artist management teams. No change to this date is anticipated; any force majeure rescheduling would trigger a full plan revision.

3. VENUE AND LAYOUT

Venue: Bayfront Event Space, Marina South (Outdoor Grounds)
Total Site Area: Approximately 12,000 sqm
Access Points: 4 public entry gates (North, East, South, West), 2 service entrances (S1, S2)

The site is divided into the following operational zones:

- Zone A: Main Stage (Meridian Stage) and main audience field
- Zone B: Second Stage (Tide Stage) and secondary audience field
- Zone C: Third Stage (Current Stage) — acoustic/electronic showcase tent
- Zone D: Food & Beverage (F&B) precinct
- Zone E: Arts Market and sponsor activation area
- Zone F: Production compound (artist holding, dressing rooms, production office)
- Zone G: Logistics and waste management holding area

A full site map with marshalling points and emergency assembly areas is appended as Annex A. All zone managers must be familiar with the location of fire extinguishers, first aid posts, and the central command post located in the Production Office (Zone F).

4. TICKETING AND ADMISSION

Ticketing is managed by our appointed ticketing partner, with all sales conducted via the official online platform. Physical box office counters will operate on event day from 10:00 to 22:00.

- Ticket types: General Admission, VIP, Group (min. 4 pax), and Artist Guest Pass.
- Entry wristbands will be issued upon scanning of the e-ticket or printed confirmation.
- Re-entry is permitted for all ticket holders, with wristband checks at each gate.
- Capacity limit for the site is 8,000 pax at any one time. Crowd counting will be coordinated by the Security Lead and reported to the Command Post every 30 minutes.

Lost or damaged wristbands will be handled at the Box Office; a replacement fee of SGD 20 applies unless the original is presented with a valid photo ID.

5. SCHEDULE OF KEY ACTIVITIES

The detailed stage-by-stage performance schedule is maintained by the Artist Liaison Lead and is distributed separately. The following are the key logistical milestones for the event day:

6. KEY PERSONNEL AND COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS
The Lumina Stage (Zone A) is the main stage for Meridian Tide Music Festival. The following schedule outlines the technical rehearsal, artist arrival, and performance times for the Lumina Stage. It is maintained by the Artist Liaison Lead and the Stage Manager, and supersedes the preliminary schedule circulated in the draft event plan (v0.4). Any further changes will be communicated via the daily production memo.

All times are in Singapore Time (SGT) and are subject to change. Final confirmations are the responsibility of the Artist Liaison Lead.

**7.1 Technical Rehearsal Schedule (Event Day, Pre-Show)**

| Time (SGT) | Activity | Responsible Party | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------------------|-------|
| 08:00 – 09:30 | Stage power-up and system check | Head of Stage & Power Vendor | Includes PA, lighting rig, and video wall. |
| 09:30 – 11:00 | Band 1 (Support Act 1) line check | Band 1 Crew, FOH Engineer | 15-minute soundcheck per channel, no full run-through. |
| 11:00 – 12:30 | Band 2 (Support Act 2) line check | Band 2 Crew, FOH Engineer | Ensure backline is swapped efficiently. |
| 12:30 – 14:00 | Headliner equipment load-in | Headliner Tour Crew | Stage is cleared of all other equipment. |
| 14:00 – 15:30 | Headliner full rehearsal (closed) | Headliner Tour Crew, FOH, Monitors | No audience. Media and VIP access strictly prohibited. |
| 15:30 – 16:00 | Headliner photo call | Artist Relations, Headliner Tour Crew | Limited to official festival photographer and approved media. |
| 16:00 – 16:30 | Stage reset for show | Stage Manager, All Crew | Final placement of risers, monitors, and cables. |
| 16:30 – 17:00 | Final safety sweep and sound check | Stage Manager, Safety Officer | Confirm all rigging points and cable runs are secure. |

**7.2 Artist Arrival and Performance Schedule**

| Time (SGT) | Artist / Act | Arrival Time (SGT) | Performance Window (SGT) | Notes |
|------------|--------------|--------------------|---------------------------|-------|
| 17:00 – 17:45 | Support Act 1 (The Sundowners) | 15:30 | 17:00 – 17:45 | 45-minute set. Load-out begins immediately after. |

| 21:00 – 22:30 | Headliner (The Crimson Tides) | 20:45 (stage call) | 21:00 – 22:30 | **Lumina Stage headliner start time is scheduled for 21:00 in the event plan. Record status: current.** This is the current confirmed time. |

*Note: The 21:00 headliner start time is a confirmed current entry in the production schedule. The earlier 20:30 start time listed in the preliminary v0.4 draft is superseded and is no longer in effect.*

**7.3 Stage Transition and Changeover Protocols**

- **Changeover Time:** A standard changeover between acts is 15 minutes. The headliner changeover is allocated 30 minutes (19:30 – 20:00) to accommodate the full stage reset.
- **Backline:** All support acts must have their backline cleared from the stage within 10 minutes of their set ending. The headliner's backline is to be placed in the wings no earlier than 14:00.
- **Set List and Cue Sheets:** Final set lists and cue sheets for the headliner must be submitted to the Stage Manager by 16:00.
- **Communication:** All stage crew will communicate via the dedicated Lumina Stage radio channel (Ch 3). The Stage Manager holds the authority to halt any transition for safety reasons.

**7.4 Additional Notes**
**7.4 Additional Notes (continued)**

The headliner's performance window is fixed and will not be extended. The Lumina Stage headliner performance duration is noted as 90 minutes in the event plan. Record status: current. This is a current controlled entry in the production schedule. Should the set overrun for any reason, the Stage Manager is to flag this immediately to the Production Director; the fireworks and drone show scheduled for 22:45 cannot be pushed later than 23:00 due to NEA permitting conditions.

The Crimson Tides have requested the following staging and technical riders, all of which have been confirmed by the artist's production manager (Ms. Priya Nair):

- **Lighting:** A dedicated follow-spot operator for the lead vocalist during the first three songs. The band's lighting director (LD) will be seated at FOH and will supply a show file; the house lighting crew will load this file during the 19:30 – 20:00 changeover and will not make any modifications without the LD's approval.
- **Sound:** The band's FOH engineer will mix from a Midas console. A 48-channel input list has been provided; the stage patch must be complete and verified by 18:00. The monitor engineer will use in-ear monitors (IEMs) for all band members; two wedge monitors are to be placed at the front edge as backup and will remain unpowered unless requested.
- **Special Effects:** The band will deploy their own CO₂ jets along the front of the stage. These are low-lying effects and will be operated by the band's own crew. The house pyrotechnician is to confirm that the CO₂ jets do not interfere with the festival's fog machine output during the final song. Any haze or fog used by the festival during the headliner set must be water-based only.
- **Stage Layout:** A riser for the drummer is required (3 ft high, 8 ft by 8 ft). The keyboard rig will be stage left; the band has requested that the monitor world be placed stage right, just off the wings. The stage carpet is to be black, non-slip, and laid no later than 15:00.

**7.5 Contingency Plans for Technical Issues**

The following contingencies are in place for the headliner's performance. These are to be read in conjunction with the main Festival Risk Assessment (Appendix C) and the Site-Specific Electrical Safety Plan (Appendix D).

| Scenario | Response | Responsible Party | Time to Implement |
|----------|----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Main PA failure (total loss of FOH sound) | Switch to the secondary PA system located on the delay towers. The headliner's FOH engineer will be notified immediately. The band has agreed to a 10-minute pause in the set if required. | Head of Sound (Mr. Kelvin Tan) | 5–10 minutes |
| Partial PA failure (one side only) | Continue the set; the monitor engineer will adjust the IEM mix to compensate. The band's FOH engineer will decide whether to pause. | FOH Engineer (band) | Immediate |
| Power failure at Lumina Stage (mains) | The generator backup (Gen Set B) will auto-start within 15 seconds. All critical audio and lighting loads are on the UPS. The band will be advised to pause for 60 seconds to allow for the transfer. | Head of Power (Mr. Rajesh Menon) | 15 seconds (auto) |
| Lighting console crash | The house lighting crew will reboot the console. A backup console is pre-programmed and can be switched over within 3 minutes. The band's LD will be informed. | Head of Lighting (Ms. Nadia Rahman) | 3 minutes |
| CO₂ jet malfunction (leak or failure) | The band's crew will isolate the affected jet. If more than two jets fail, the band may choose to continue without them; no change to the set duration. | Band's Crew Chief | 2–5 minutes |
| Drummer riser instability | The stage crew will secure the riser with additional bracing. If the riser cannot be made safe, the drums will be moved to the stage floor. The band's crew will assist. | Stage Manager (Mr. Derek Chua) | 5 minutes |
| Monitor failure (IEMs) | The backup wedges will be powered on. The monitor engineer will switch the affected channel to the wedge mix. | Monitor Engineer | 1–2 minutes |
## 6. CROWD MANAGEMENT AND PUBLIC SAFETY

### 6.1 Crowd Density Targets

The following density targets apply to all public areas and are to be monitored by the Crowd Management Team via the CCTV control room and floor spotters. These targets assume normal weather conditions.

| Zone | Max Density (persons per sq m) | Max Occupancy | Notes |
|------|-------------------------------|---------------|-------|
| Main Stage viewing area (front of FOH) | 4 | 4,500 | Reduced to 3 if wet weather is forecast |
| Main Stage viewing area (rear of FOH) | 3 | 3,000 | |
| Lumina Stage viewing area | 3 | 1,800 | |
| Food Village | 2 | 1,200 | Includes seating areas |
| Wellness Zone | 2 | 800 | |
| Walkways (all) | 2 | n/a | Flow rate monitored |
| Chill-out Zone (near Bay Entrance) | 2 | 600 | |
| Merchandise & Information tent | 2 | 300 | |

If any zone exceeds its maximum density for more than 10 minutes, the Crowd Management Team will implement the following, in order:

1.  Close the zone to new entries (gate stewards to redirect).
2.  Increase the frequency of PA announcements advising patrons to move to less crowded areas.
3.  Open secondary access/egress routes (if available for that zone).
4.  For the Main Stage viewing area only: implement a temporary one-way flow system from the rear of the crowd.

The Festival Director (or, in their absence, the Head of Crowd Management) has the authority to stop the performance at the Main Stage or Lumina Stage if crowd density cannot be brought back within target after 15 minutes of implementing the above measures. This is a last resort.

### 6.2 Crowd Management Staffing

Crowd management is provided by a licensed security agency (Sentinel Security Services Pte Ltd) under the supervision of the Head of Crowd Management, Ms. Farah Binte Ismail.

| Location | Number of Stewards | Shifts |

| Main Stage viewing area | 24 | 2 shifts (12 hrs each) |
| Lumina Stage viewing area | 12 | 2 shifts |

| Walkways / roaming | 10 | 2 shifts |

| Chill-out Zone | 4 | 2 shifts |
| Merchandise & Information tent | 4 | 2 shifts |
| Backstage / artist compound | 6 | 2 shifts |

All stewards will report to the Crowd Management Control Point (CP-2) located near the Bay Entrance. Shift changeover is at 1400 hrs and 0200 hrs. The Head of Crowd Management will conduct a briefing at the start of each shift.

### 6.3 Lost & Found and Missing Persons

- The Lost & Found point is located at the Information Tent (adjacent to the Merchandise tent).
- Parents/guardians of missing children should be directed to the Information Tent immediately.
- A dedicated radio channel (Ch 6) is reserved for missing person alerts. The Control Room will broadcast a description of the missing person on this channel and on the PA system if requested.
- If a missing person is not located within 30 minutes, the Control Room will notify the Singapore Police Force via the Festival Security Liaison Officer.

## 7. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

### 7.1 Medical Emergencies

- First aid is provided by two on-site medical teams (Red Cross Singapore volunteers) at Medical Post 1 (near the Main Stage) and Medical Post 2 (near the Food Village).
- Each medical post is staffed by at least 2 first aiders at all times. An ambulance is stationed on-site at the West Service Road from 1600 hrs each day until 30 minutes after the programme ends.
- All medical incidents are to be logged by the Control Room. The log will record: time, location, nature of injury/illness, treatment provided, and disposition.
- For serious incidents (e.g. cardiac arrest, suspected spinal injury, severe bleeding), the Control Room will call 995 immediately and direct the ambulance to the nearest service gate.

Event: Marina Bay Music Festival (MTMF)

Prepared by: Safety Committee
Date of issue: 12 August 2026 (post-event)

1. Purpose and Scope
This report consolidates crowd safety and compliance data for the Marina Bay Music Festival held on 11 August 2026 at the Marina Bay Promenade. It covers pre-event planning, live monitoring, and post-event review. All references to capacity limits, hazard assessments, and crowd density estimates are based on the festival’s Safety Management Plan (SMP) and on-site telemetry logs.

2. Stage Capacity and Compliance
2.1 Controlled Capacities (Current)
The following maximum capacities are in effect for the current festival edition and were used as the basis for all ticketing, barrier setup, and crowd flow planning.

| Stage | Max Capacity (people) | Status |
|-------|------------------------|--------|
| Lumina Stage | 8000 | Current (controlled entry) |
| Bayfront Stage | 4500 | Current (controlled entry) |
| Harbour Stage | 2500 | Current (controlled entry) |

Lumina Stage max capacity is set at 8000 people per the safety report. Record status: current. This figure was derived from the stage’s viewing area, egress routes, and fire engine access lanes. It was reviewed by the Safety Committee on 1 August 2026 and remains valid for the current festival edition.

2.2 Capacity Enforcement
- Ticketing: Entry to Lumina Stage was managed via wristband allocation. A maximum of 8000 wristbands were issued for the Lumina Zone.
- Real-time counting: Turnstile counters and CCTV-based density analytics were used. At 20:15, the Lumina Stage counted crowd reached 7,840, triggering a Level 2 alert (see Section 4.2).
- Barrier management: If the count exceeds 95% of capacity (7,600), entry gates are closed temporarily. This was activated at 20:12 and again at 21:30.

2.3 Superseded Information
An earlier draft of the SMP (dated 15 July 2026) proposed a higher capacity of 9,000 for Lumina Stage. This was superseded on 28 July 2026 after a re-assessment of the exit route from the east lawn. The 9,000 figure is no longer valid and should not be used for any planning or compliance purposes. All current documents reference the 8,000 figure.

3. Crowd Density Estimates
Density estimates were recorded at 15-minute intervals from 16:00 to 23:00. Estimates are based on CCTV grid sampling and manual spot checks. Values are approximate and may have a margin of error of ±10%.

4. Hazard Assessments and Incident Log
4.1 Pre-event Hazard Assessment (Summary)
Completed on 5 August 2026. Key hazards identified:
- HZ-04: Crowd surge near Lumina Stage barriers during high-demand acts.
- HZ-07: Trip hazards from loose cabling along the east lawn.
- HZ-11: Heat stress risk, with forecast temperatures above 31°C.

Mitigations: Additional barriers at Lumina, cable ramps installed, and extra water stations (total 8) deployed.
MTMF Safety Report – Crowd Safety and Compliance

4.2 Secondary Stage Capacity and Crowd Flow Management

The three secondary stages (Sonic Grove, Bayfront, Harbour) operate under separate capacity limits from the main Lumina Stage. These limits are set by the Safety Committee and reviewed annually or after any significant incident.

Table 4.2-1: Current Stage Capacities

| Stage | Capacity (people) | Notes |
|-------|-------------------|-------|
| Lumina Stage | 8,000 | Main stage; includes east lawn viewing area |
| Bayfront Stage | 3,500 | Standing only; two exit lanes to Bayfront Ave |
| Sonic Grove Stage | 5,000 | Secondary stage; see Section 4.2.1 |
| Harbour Stage | 2,000 | Smallest stage; limited by pier access width |

Sonic Grove Stage max capacity is listed as 5000 people in the safety report. Record status: current. This figure was confirmed during the 28 July 2026 capacity re-assessment and remains current as of the event date. It is based on the stage's location on the west lawn, which provides a wider egress corridor than the east lawn route used by Lumina Stage. The 5,000 figure was first adopted in the SMP v4.2 (28 July 2026) and has not been revised since.

4.2.1 Sonic Grove Stage – Specific Controls

Sonic Grove is located at the west end of the festival grounds, adjacent to the secondary entry gate (Gate C). Its layout differs from Lumina in three key respects:

- The viewing area is a single rectangular plot (approx. 55m x 45m) with no tiered sections.
- There are two exit routes: Route A (north, 12m wide) to the West Carpark, and Route B (south, 8m wide) to the Riverside Walk.
- The stage is fully covered by a tensile canopy; this reduces heat exposure but also limits natural ventilation.

Crowd flow management for Sonic Grove follows the same principles as Lumina but with adjusted thresholds due to the smaller footprint. The key control is the holding area located 40m west of the stage, which can hold up to 1,200 people before it reaches its own limit. When the main viewing area reaches 4,200 people (85% of capacity), the holding area is opened and entry is managed on a one-in-one-out basis. This procedure was activated twice during the event:

- First activation at 18:45 (during artist changeover at Lumina, which drew a secondary crowd to Sonic Grove).
- Second activation at 21:10 (during the final act at Sonic Grove, which was the only stage still running).

No full closure of Sonic Grove was required. The highest recorded count at Sonic Grove was 4,800 people at 21:15, which is below the 5,000 capacity but above the 85% threshold. This count was verified by two independent spot checks (CCTV grid and manual clicker) with a discrepancy of 40 people (0.8%), which is within the acceptable tolerance of ±2%.

4.2.2 Crowd Flow Measures at Secondary Stages

In addition to the capacity limits, the following crowd flow measures were in place at all secondary stages:

- Entry/exit signage: Directional arrows were placed at 5m intervals along the main walking routes. A post-event audit found 3 signs missing at Harbour Stage (see Incident Log, INC-2026-08-09-014).
- Barrier layout: Bayfront and Sonic Grove used a mix of fixed steel barriers and water-filled barriers. Harbour Stage used only steel barriers due to the narrow pier.
- Staffing: Each secondary stage had a minimum of 4 crowd management staff plus 1 supervisor. This was increased to 6 staff during peak hours (19:00–22:00) at Sonic Grove and Bayfront.
- Communication: All crowd management staff carried two-way radios on Channel 3 (secondary stages) and Channel 1 (command). A radio check was conducted every 30 minutes.

A specific risk identified during the pre-event assessment was the potential for crowd mixing between Lumina and Sonic Grove during peak periods. The two stages are separated by approx. 200m of open lawn, but there is no physical barrier between them. To mitigate this, a dedicated "transit lane" was marked with ground tape, and staff were instructed to keep this lane clear. This measure was effective, with no reported congestion in the transit lane during the event.

**7. Overall Safety Compliance Summary**

The Marina Bay Music Festival (MTMF) 2026 was held on 8 March 2026 across three stages (Lumina, Sonic Grove, Harbour) with an estimated total attendance of 18,400 pax. The event was conducted in accordance with the approved Event Safety Plan (ESP-2026-03-08-01) and the supplementary risk assessments. No major incidents (Class 1 or Class 2) were recorded. A total of 24 minor incidents were logged, all of which were resolved on-site without requiring external medical transport or escalation to the Singapore Civil Defence Force.

Compliance with the licensed capacity and crowd density parameters was maintained throughout the event. The peak crowd density of 2.3 people/m² at Lumina Stage (21:45) was within the short-duration acceptable range defined in RA-2026-03-08-02. No crowd surges, compression events, or barrier failures were reported.

| Major incidents (Class 1 & 2) | 0 | 0 | Compliant |

**8. Incident Trend Analysis**

The 24 minor incidents recorded during MTMF 2026 were categorised as follows:

**Table 8.1: Incident Breakdown by Type**

| Incident Type | Count | Notes |
|---------------|-------|-------|
| Slips, trips, and falls | 9 | Majority on uneven ground near stage barriers; no serious injuries |

No incident required escalation to the on-site medical lead beyond routine first aid. The most common contributing factor for the slips and trips was the transition between paved walkways and the temporary ground protection mats used in the viewing areas. This has been noted as a recommendation for future events (see Section 10).

3.3 All equipment shall be transported in appropriate flight cases with clear labelling. The Vendor is responsible for all costs associated with transport, insurance, and customs clearance (if applicable).

4. PAYMENT TERMS

4.1 Total contract value: SGD 148,500.00 (excluding GST).

4.2 Payment schedule:

- 20% deposit (SGD 29,700.00) upon contract execution
- 40% (SGD 59,400.00) upon delivery of equipment to site on 10 June 2024
- 40% (SGD 59,400.00) within 30 days of successful completion of services and submission of final invoice

4.3 All invoices shall be submitted in Singapore dollars. GST shall be applied at the prevailing rate.

4.4 Late payment: The Client shall pay interest at 1.5% per month on any amount overdue beyond 30 days from invoice date.

5.1 The Vendor shall ensure that all equipment meets the specifications set out in Schedule A and operates in accordance with manufacturer specifications throughout the festival.
5.2 The Vendor shall provide a minimum of four (4) qualified technical staff on site during the festival operational days, comprising at least one (1) system engineer, two (2) audio technicians, and one (1) RF coordinator. Staff shall be present from 08:00 to 23:00 daily during the festival period, or such other times as reasonably required by the Client for technical rehearsals and load-out.

5.3 The Vendor shall maintain a spare parts and backup equipment inventory on site at all times during the festival operational days. The minimum backup inventory shall include, but not be limited to:

- 1 x console (matching the FOH console model)

- 1 x wireless bodypack transmitter
- 2 x microphone capsules (dynamic and condenser)

5.4 The Vendor shall provide 24-hour technical support via telephone and email from the date of equipment delivery until completion of load-out. Response time for critical issues shall be within 30 minutes during operational hours and within 2 hours outside operational hours.

6. MAINTENANCE AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE

6.1 Routine maintenance: The Vendor shall perform daily system checks prior to gates opening on each operational day. Checks shall include console health, signal flow verification, wireless frequency scans, and amplifier status. 6.2 Emergency response: In the event of equipment failure during the festival operational days, the Vendor shall:

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This Event Plan defines the overall framework for the staging of the Meridian Tide Music Festival (MTMF) 2026. It consolidates the confirmed schedule, key logistics, venue layout, ticketing operations, and vendor coordination responsibilities. This document serves as the reference point for all production, operations, and external partners for the duration of the planning cycle and the event itself.

All times referenced in this plan are in Singapore Time (SGT) and use the 24-hour format. Any deviation from this plan requires written approval from the Production Director and must be logged as an addendum to this document.

2. EVENT OVERVIEW

The Meridian Tide Music Festival is an annual multi-stage music event showcasing regional and international acts. The 2026 edition aims to deliver a seamless audience experience across three performance stages, a dedicated food and beverage precinct, and an integrated arts market. The festival's core mission is to provide a platform for emerging Southeast Asian artists while maintaining a high standard of production safety and operational efficiency.

The Meridian Tide Music Festival event date is confirmed as 2026-03-14 in the event plan. Record status: current. This date has been locked with all key stakeholders, including the venue operator, major sponsors, and artist management teams. No change to this date is anticipated; any force majeure rescheduling would trigger a full plan revision.

3. VENUE AND LAYOUT

Venue: Bayfront Event Space, Marina South (Outdoor Grounds)
Total Site Area: Approximately 12,000 sqm
Access Points: 4 public entry gates (North, East, South, West), 2 service entrances (S1, S2)

The site is divided into the following operational zones:

- Zone A: Main Stage (Meridian Stage) and main audience field
- Zone B: Second Stage (Tide Stage) and secondary audience field
- Zone C: Third Stage (Current Stage) — acoustic/electronic showcase tent
- Zone D: Food & Beverage (F&B) precinct
- Zone E: Arts Market and sponsor activation area
- Zone F: Production compound (artist holding, dressing rooms, production office)
- Zone G: Logistics and waste management holding area

A full site map with marshalling points and emergency assembly areas is appended as Annex A. All zone managers must be familiar with the location of fire extinguishers, first aid posts, and the central command post located in the Production Office (Zone F).

4. TICKETING AND ADMISSION

Ticketing is managed by our appointed ticketing partner, with all sales conducted via the official online platform. Physical box office counters will operate on event day from 10:00 to 22:00.

- Ticket types: General Admission, VIP, Group (min. 4 pax), and Artist Guest Pass.
- Entry wristbands will be issued upon scanning of the e-ticket or printed confirmation.
- Re-entry is permitted for all ticket holders, with wristband checks at each gate.
- Capacity limit for the site is 8,000 pax at any one time. Crowd counting will be coordinated by the Security Lead and reported to the Command Post every 30 minutes.

Lost or damaged wristbands will be handled at the Box Office; a replacement fee of SGD 20 applies unless the original is presented with a valid photo ID.

5. SCHEDULE OF KEY ACTIVITIES

The detailed stage-by-stage performance schedule is maintained by the Artist Liaison Lead and is distributed separately. The following are the key logistical milestones for the event day:

6. KEY PERSONNEL AND COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS

**7.4 Additional Notes (continued)**

The headliner's performance window is fixed and will not be extended. The Lumina Stage headliner performance duration is noted as 90 minutes in the event plan. Record status: current. This is a current controlled entry in the production schedule. Should the set overrun for any reason, the Stage Manager is to flag this immediately to the Production Director; the fireworks and drone show scheduled for 22:45 cannot be pushed later than 23:00 due to NEA permitting conditions.

The Crimson Tides have requested the following staging and technical riders, all of which have been confirmed by the artist's production manager (Ms. Priya Nair):

- **Lighting:** A dedicated follow-spot operator for the lead vocalist during the first three songs. The band's lighting director (LD) will be seated at FOH and will supply a show file; the house lighting crew will load this file during the 19:30 – 20:00 changeover and will not make any modifications without the LD's approval.
- **Sound:** The band's FOH engineer will mix from a Midas console. A 48-channel input list has been provided; the stage patch must be complete and verified by 18:00. The monitor engineer will use in-ear monitors (IEMs) for all band members; two wedge monitors are to be placed at the front edge as backup and will remain unpowered unless requested.
- **Special Effects:** The band will deploy their own CO₂ jets along the front of the stage. These are low-lying effects and will be operated by the band's own crew. The house pyrotechnician is to confirm that the CO₂ jets do not interfere with the festival's fog machine output during the final song. Any haze or fog used by the festival during the headliner set must be water-based only.
- **Stage Layout:** A riser for the drummer is required (3 ft high, 8 ft by 8 ft). The keyboard rig will be stage left; the band has requested that the monitor world be placed stage right, just off the wings. The stage carpet is to be black, non-slip, and laid no later than 15:00.

**7.5 Contingency Plans for Technical Issues**

The following contingencies are in place for the headliner's performance. These are to be read in conjunction with the main Festival Risk Assessment (Appendix C) and the Site-Specific Electrical Safety Plan (Appendix D).

| Scenario | Response | Responsible Party | Time to Implement |
|----------|----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Main PA failure (total loss of FOH sound) | Switch to the secondary PA system located on the delay towers. The headliner's FOH engineer will be notified immediately. The band has agreed to a 10-minute pause in the set if required. | Head of Sound (Mr. Kelvin Tan) | 5–10 minutes |
| Partial PA failure (one side only) | Continue the set; the monitor engineer will adjust the IEM mix to compensate. The band's FOH engineer will decide whether to pause. | FOH Engineer (band) | Immediate |
| Power failure at Lumina Stage (mains) | The generator backup (Gen Set B) will auto-start within 15 seconds. All critical audio and lighting loads are on the UPS. The band will be advised to pause for 60 seconds to allow for the transfer. | Head of Power (Mr. Rajesh Menon) | 15 seconds (auto) |
| Lighting console crash | The house lighting crew will reboot the console. A backup console is pre-programmed and can be switched over within 3 minutes. The band's LD will be informed. | Head of Lighting (Ms. Nadia Rahman) | 3 minutes |
| CO₂ jet malfunction (leak or failure) | The band's crew will isolate the affected jet. If more than two jets fail, the band may choose to continue without them; no change to the set duration. | Band's Crew Chief | 2–5 minutes |
| Drummer riser instability | The stage crew will secure the riser with additional bracing. If the riser cannot be made safe, the drums will be moved to the stage floor. The band's crew will assist. | Stage Manager (Mr. Derek Chua) | 5 minutes |
| Monitor failure (IEMs) | The backup wedges will be powered on. The monitor engineer will switch the affected channel to the wedge mix. | Monitor Engineer | 1–2 minutes |

## 6. CROWD MANAGEMENT AND PUBLIC SAFETY

### 6.1 Crowd Density Targets

The following density targets apply to all public areas and are to be monitored by the Crowd Management Team via the CCTV control room and floor spotters. These targets assume normal weather conditions.

| Zone | Max Density (persons per sq m) | Max Occupancy | Notes |
|------|-------------------------------|---------------|-------|
| Main Stage viewing area (front of FOH) | 4 | 4,500 | Reduced to 3 if wet weather is forecast |
| Main Stage viewing area (rear of FOH) | 3 | 3,000 | |
| Lumina Stage viewing area | 3 | 1,800 | |
| Food Village | 2 | 1,200 | Includes seating areas |
| Wellness Zone | 2 | 800 | |
| Walkways (all) | 2 | n/a | Flow rate monitored |
| Chill-out Zone (near Bay Entrance) | 2 | 600 | |
| Merchandise & Information tent | 2 | 300 | |

If any zone exceeds its maximum density for more than 10 minutes, the Crowd Management Team will implement the following, in order:

1.  Close the zone to new entries (gate stewards to redirect).
2.  Increase the frequency of PA announcements advising patrons to move to less crowded areas.
3.  Open secondary access/egress routes (if available for that zone).
4.  For the Main Stage viewing area only: implement a temporary one-way flow system from the rear of the crowd.

The Festival Director (or, in their absence, the Head of Crowd Management) has the authority to stop the performance at the Main Stage or Lumina Stage if crowd density cannot be brought back within target after 15 minutes of implementing the above measures. This is a last resort.

### 6.2 Crowd Management Staffing

Crowd management is provided by a licensed security agency (Sentinel Security Services Pte Ltd) under the supervision of the Head of Crowd Management, Ms. Farah Binte Ismail.

| Location | Number of Stewards | Shifts |
|----------|--------------------|--------|
| Main Stage viewing area | 24 | 2 shifts (12 hrs each) |
| Lumina Stage viewing area | 12 | 2 shifts |
| Bay Entrance / ticketing | 18 | 2 shifts |
| Food Village | 8 | 2 shifts |
| Walkways / roaming | 10 | 2 shifts |
| Wellness Zone | 4 | 2 shifts |
| Chill-out Zone | 4 | 2 shifts |
| Merchandise & Information tent | 4 | 2 shifts |
| Backstage / artist compound | 6 | 2 shifts |
| **Total** | **90** | |

All stewards will report to the Crowd Management Control Point (CP-2) located near the Bay Entrance. Shift changeover is at 1400 hrs and 0200 hrs. The Head of Crowd Management will conduct a briefing at the start of each shift.

### 6.3 Lost & Found and Missing Persons

- The Lost & Found point is located at the Information Tent (adjacent to the Merchandise tent).
- Parents/guardians of missing children should be directed to the Information Tent immediately.
- A dedicated radio channel (Ch 6) is reserved for missing person alerts. The Control Room will broadcast a description of the missing person on this channel and on the PA system if requested.
- If a missing person is not located within 30 minutes, the Control Room will notify the Singapore Police Force via the Festival Security Liaison Officer.

## 7. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

### 7.1 Medical Emergencies

- First aid is provided by two on-site medical teams (Red Cross Singapore volunteers) at Medical Post 1 (near the Main Stage) and Medical Post 2 (near the Food Village).
- Each medical post is staffed by at least 2 first aiders at all times. An ambulance is stationed on-site at the West Service Road from 1600 hrs each day until 30 minutes after the programme ends.
- All medical incidents are to be logged by the Control Room. The log will record: time, location, nature of injury/illness, treatment provided, and disposition.
- For serious incidents (e.g. cardiac arrest, suspected spinal injury, severe bleeding), the Control Room will call 995 immediately and direct the ambulance to the nearest service gate.

MTMF Safety Report – Crowd Safety and Compliance
Event: Marina Bay Music Festival (MTMF)
Report ID: MTMF-SAF-2026-0811
Prepared by: Safety Committee
Date of issue: 12 August 2026 (post-event)

1. Purpose and Scope
This report consolidates crowd safety and compliance data for the Marina Bay Music Festival held on 11 August 2026 at the Marina Bay Promenade. It covers pre-event planning, live monitoring, and post-event review. All references to capacity limits, hazard assessments, and crowd density estimates are based on the festival’s Safety Management Plan (SMP) and on-site telemetry logs.

2. Stage Capacity and Compliance
2.1 Controlled Capacities (Current)
The following maximum capacities are in effect for the current festival edition and were used as the basis for all ticketing, barrier setup, and crowd flow planning.

| Stage | Max Capacity (people) | Status |
|-------|------------------------|--------|
| Lumina Stage | 8000 | Current (controlled entry) |
| Bayfront Stage | 4500 | Current (controlled entry) |
| Harbour Stage | 2500 | Current (controlled entry) |

Lumina Stage max capacity is set at 8000 people per the safety report. Record status: current. This figure was derived from the stage’s viewing area, egress routes, and fire engine access lanes. It was reviewed by the Safety Committee on 1 August 2026 and remains valid for the current festival edition.

2.2 Capacity Enforcement
- Ticketing: Entry to Lumina Stage was managed via wristband allocation. A maximum of 8000 wristbands were issued for the Lumina Zone.
- Real-time counting: Turnstile counters and CCTV-based density analytics were used. At 20:15, the Lumina Stage counted crowd reached 7,840, triggering a Level 2 alert (see Section 4.2).
- Barrier management: If the count exceeds 95% of capacity (7,600), entry gates are closed temporarily. This was activated at 20:12 and again at 21:30.

2.3 Superseded Information
An earlier draft of the SMP (dated 15 July 2026) proposed a higher capacity of 9,000 for Lumina Stage. This was superseded on 28 July 2026 after a re-assessment of the exit route from the east lawn. The 9,000 figure is no longer valid and should not be used for any planning or compliance purposes. All current documents reference the 8,000 figure.

3. Crowd Density Estimates
Density estimates were recorded at 15-minute intervals from 16:00 to 23:00. Estimates are based on CCTV grid sampling and manual spot checks. Values are approximate and may have a margin of error of ±10%.

| Time | Lumina Stage (people) | Density (per sq m) | Bayfront Stage (people) | Harbour Stage (people) |
|------|------------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|
| 16:00 | 1,200 | 0.3 | 400 | 150 |
| 17:00 | 2,800 | 0.7 | 1,100 | 300 |
| 18:00 | 4,500 | 1.1 | 2,000 | 600 |
| 19:00 | 6,100 | 1.5 | 3,100 | 1,100 |
| 20:00 | 7,300 | 1.8 | 3,900 | 1,800 |
| 21:00 | 7,900 | 2.0 | 4,200 | 2,200 |
| 22:00 | 7,600 | 1.9 | 3,800 | 2,000 |
| 23:00 | 5,200 | 1.3 | 2,500 | 1,200 |

Note: Density per sq m is calculated for the main viewing area of each stage. At 21:00, the Lumina Stage density reached 2.0 per sq m, which is the upper limit for a standing crowd with active music (Level 3). No density data was recorded for the VIP deck at Lumina Stage due to a camera fault between 19:30 and 20:45.

4. Hazard Assessments and Incident Log
4.1 Pre-event Hazard Assessment (Summary)
Completed on 5 August 2026. Key hazards identified:
- HZ-04: Crowd surge near Lumina Stage barriers during high-demand acts.
- HZ-07: Trip hazards from loose cabling along the east lawn.
- HZ-11: Heat stress risk, with forecast temperatures above 31°C.

Mitigations: Additional barriers at Lumina, cable ramps installed, and extra water stations (total 8) deployed.

4.2 Secondary Stage Capacity and Crowd Flow Management

The three secondary stages (Sonic Grove, Bayfront, Harbour) operate under separate capacity limits from the main Lumina Stage. These limits are set by the Safety Committee and reviewed annually or after any significant incident.

Table 4.2-1: Current Stage Capacities

| Stage | Capacity (people) | Notes |
|-------|-------------------|-------|
| Lumina Stage | 8,000 | Main stage; includes east lawn viewing area |
| Bayfront Stage | 3,500 | Standing only; two exit lanes to Bayfront Ave |
| Sonic Grove Stage | 5,000 | Secondary stage; see Section 4.2.1 |
| Harbour Stage | 2,000 | Smallest stage; limited by pier access width |

Sonic Grove Stage max capacity is listed as 5000 people in the safety report. Record status: current. This figure was confirmed during the 28 July 2026 capacity re-assessment and remains current as of the event date. It is based on the stage's location on the west lawn, which provides a wider egress corridor than the east lawn route used by Lumina Stage. The 5,000 figure was first adopted in the SMP v4.2 (28 July 2026) and has not been revised since.

4.2.1 Sonic Grove Stage – Specific Controls

Sonic Grove is located at the west end of the festival grounds, adjacent to the secondary entry gate (Gate C). Its layout differs from Lumina in three key respects:

- The viewing area is a single rectangular plot (approx. 55m x 45m) with no tiered sections.
- There are two exit routes: Route A (north, 12m wide) to the West Carpark, and Route B (south, 8m wide) to the Riverside Walk.
- The stage is fully covered by a tensile canopy; this reduces heat exposure but also limits natural ventilation.

Crowd flow management for Sonic Grove follows the same principles as Lumina but with adjusted thresholds due to the smaller footprint. The key control is the holding area located 40m west of the stage, which can hold up to 1,200 people before it reaches its own limit. When the main viewing area reaches 4,200 people (85% of capacity), the holding area is opened and entry is managed on a one-in-one-out basis. This procedure was activated twice during the event:

- First activation at 18:45 (during artist changeover at Lumina, which drew a secondary crowd to Sonic Grove).
- Second activation at 21:10 (during the final act at Sonic Grove, which was the only stage still running).

No full closure of Sonic Grove was required. The highest recorded count at Sonic Grove was 4,800 people at 21:15, which is below the 5,000 capacity but above the 85% threshold. This count was verified by two independent spot checks (CCTV grid and manual clicker) with a discrepancy of 40 people (0.8%), which is within the acceptable tolerance of ±2%.

4.2.2 Crowd Flow Measures at Secondary Stages

In addition to the capacity limits, the following crowd flow measures were in place at all secondary stages:

- Entry/exit signage: Directional arrows were placed at 5m intervals along the main walking routes. A post-event audit found 3 signs missing at Harbour Stage (see Incident Log, INC-2026-08-09-014).
- Barrier layout: Bayfront and Sonic Grove used a mix of fixed steel barriers and water-filled barriers. Harbour Stage used only steel barriers due to the narrow pier.
- Staffing: Each secondary stage had a minimum of 4 crowd management staff plus 1 supervisor. This was increased to 6 staff during peak hours (19:00–22:00) at Sonic Grove and Bayfront.
- Communication: All crowd management staff carried two-way radios on Channel 3 (secondary stages) and Channel 1 (command). A radio check was conducted every 30 minutes.

A specific risk identified during the pre-event assessment was the potential for crowd mixing between Lumina and Sonic Grove during peak periods. The two stages are separated by approx. 200m of open lawn, but there is no physical barrier between them. To mitigate this, a dedicated "transit lane" was marked with ground tape, and staff were instructed to keep this lane clear. This measure was effective, with no reported congestion in the transit lane during the event.

- Lumina Stage: 2.3 people/m² (peak, short-duration)
- Sonic Grove: 1.4 people/m² (comfortable standing)
- Harbour Stage: 0.8 people/m² (low density)

*Note: Density calculations are based on the designated viewing area dimensions provided in the site layout plan (SLP-2026-03-08-01). Actual usable area may vary slightly due to barrier placement and stage equipment.*

---

**6. Crowd Flow and Transit Lane Observations**

The transit lane between Lumina Stage and Sonic Grove remained clear throughout the event. At 21:45, the lane was observed to have a steady flow of attendees moving between stages, with no bottlenecks or congestion reported.

At 22:20, a minor congestion point was observed at the junction of the transit lane and Exit Corridor C. This was attributed to the end of the Harbour Stage performance and the subsequent movement of attendees toward the main exit. Staff directed the crowd to the alternate exit (Exit Corridor B), and the congestion resolved within 10 minutes.

**Table 6.1: Transit Lane Observations**

| Time (SGT) | Location | Observation | Action Taken |
|------------|----------|-------------|--------------|
| 21:45 | Transit Lane (Lumina–Sonic Grove) | Clear flow; no congestion | Routine monitoring |
| 22:20 | Junction with Exit Corridor C | Minor congestion due to Harbour Stage exit | Staff redirected crowd to alternate exit; resolved by 22:30 |
| 22:50 | Transit Lane (Lumina–Sonic Grove) | Reduced flow; event winding down | Routine monitoring |

**MTMF Safety Report – Crowd Safety and Compliance**
**Post-Event Summary and Recommendations**
**File Ref: MTMF-SR-2026-004**
**Date of Issue: 12 March 2026**
**Prepared by: Safety Committee, Marina Bay Music Festival (MTMF)**

---

**7. Overall Safety Compliance Summary**

The Marina Bay Music Festival (MTMF) 2026 was held on 8 March 2026 across three stages (Lumina, Sonic Grove, Harbour) with an estimated total attendance of 18,400 pax. The event was conducted in accordance with the approved Event Safety Plan (ESP-2026-03-08-01) and the supplementary risk assessments. No major incidents (Class 1 or Class 2) were recorded. A total of 24 minor incidents were logged, all of which were resolved on-site without requiring external medical transport or escalation to the Singapore Civil Defence Force.

Compliance with the licensed capacity and crowd density parameters was maintained throughout the event. The peak crowd density of 2.3 people/m² at Lumina Stage (21:45) was within the short-duration acceptable range defined in RA-2026-03-08-02. No crowd surges, compression events, or barrier failures were reported.

**Table 7.1: Overall Compliance Metrics**

| Metric | Target / Standard | Recorded | Status |
|--------|-------------------|----------|--------|
| Licensed capacity | 20,000 pax | 18,400 pax (peak) | Compliant |
| Peak crowd density (Lumina Stage) | ≤ 2.0 comfortable; ≤ 2.5 short-duration peak | 2.3 people/m² (21:45) | Compliant (short-duration) |
| First aid consultations | N/A | 31 | No hospital referrals |
| Minor incidents (Class 3) | N/A | 24 | All resolved on-site |
| Major incidents (Class 1 & 2) | 0 | 0 | Compliant |
| Transit lane congestion events | ≤ 3 | 1 (resolved in 10 min) | Compliant |

---

**8. Incident Trend Analysis**

The 24 minor incidents recorded during MTMF 2026 were categorised as follows:

**Table 8.1: Incident Breakdown by Type**

| Incident Type | Count | Notes |
|---------------|-------|-------|
| Slips, trips, and falls | 9 | Majority on uneven ground near stage barriers; no serious injuries |
| Heat-related discomfort | 6 | Treated at first aid posts; all discharged after hydration and rest |
| Minor cuts and abrasions | 4 | Treated with dressings on-site |
| Lost persons (reunited) | 3 | All reunited with parties within 30 minutes |
| Other (e.g., minor allergic reactions, dizziness) | 2 | Resolved at first aid posts |

No incident required escalation to the on-site medical lead beyond routine first aid. The most common contributing factor for the slips and trips was the transition between paved walkways and the temporary ground protection mats used in the viewing areas. This has been noted as a recommendation for future events (see Section 10).

---

**9. Final Crowd Counts and Safety Metrics**

The final attendance figures were consolidated from entry gate counts, wristband issuance, and exit counts. The peak concurrent attendance was recorded at 21:45 SGT, corresponding to the headlining performance at Lumina Stage.

**Table 9.1: Final Attendance and Density Figures**

| Location | Peak Concurrent Count | Viewing Area (m²) | Density (people/m²) | Status |
|----------|-----------------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------|
| Lumina Stage | 7,820 | 3,400 | 2.3 | Acceptable (short-duration peak) |
| Sonic Grove | 4,200 | 3,000 | 1.4 | Comfortable standing |
| Harbour Stage | 1,600 | 2,000 | 0.8 | Low density |
| Food & Retail Village | 2,300 | 1,800 | 1.3 | Comfortable standing |
| Transit lanes / common areas | 2,480 | N/A | N/A | No congestion |

*Total peak concurrent attendance: 18,400 pax (21:45 SGT).*

The exit flow was monitored from 22:30 onwards. The main exit (Exit Corridor A) handled the majority of the outbound flow. The alternate exits (Exit Corridor B and C) were utilised without reported bottlenecks. The full site was cleared by 23:50 SGT, within the planned 60-minute clearance window.

VENDOR CONTRACT – SKYLINE AUDIO EQUIPMENT AND SERVICES

Contract No.: SA-2024-0118
Prepared: 18 January 2024
Effective Date: 1 March 2024
Parties: Lumina Festival Pte. Ltd. ("Client") and Skyline Audio Pte. Ltd. ("Vendor")

1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Vendor shall supply, deliver, install, test, and operate the sound reinforcement system for the Lumina Stage (the "Stage") during the Lumina Music Festival 2024, scheduled for 14–16 June 2024 at the Bayfront Event Grounds, Singapore. Services include:

a) Provision of the main PA system, front-of-house (FOH) and monitor consoles, outboard processing, cabling, and all ancillary equipment listed in Schedule A;

b) On-site engineering and operational support for the duration of the festival, including load-in, rehearsals, performances, and load-out;

c) A dedicated system technician on standby for the full festival period, including non-performance hours;

d) Pre-event system tuning and acoustical alignment, subject to site access and weather conditions;

e) Provision of spare components, backup consoles, and emergency technical support.

2. EQUIPMENT SPECIFICATION

2.1 Main Sound System. The Lumina Stage sound system model is specified as LineX Array 3 in the vendor contract. Record status: current. The system comprises the following primary components:

- Main left/right arrays: 16 x LineX Array 3 loudspeaker cabinets per side
- Subwoofer arrays: 12 x LX-SUB218 dual 18" subwoofers
- Front fills: 6 x LX-FILL12 compact loudspeakers
- Outfill/delay: 8 x LX-FILL12 (additional, for side coverage)
- Amplification: LineX D80 four-channel amplifiers (total 32 units)

2.2 Consoles and Processing.

- FOH console: Yamaha Rivage PM7 digital console (1 unit, with redundant engine)
- Monitor console: Digico SD7 Quantum (1 unit)
- System processor: LineX DX44 system controller (4 units)
- Stage racks: 2 x LineX RACK8 with IO panels

2.3 Cabling and Distribution.

- LOOM: 250 m of 12-pair audio snake (2 runs)
- Power distribution: 63A 3-phase distribution boards (4 units)
- Ethernet cabling for console networking: 6 x 100 m CAT6 shielded

2.4 All equipment shall be delivered in good working order, with current firmware versions installed and verified by the Vendor prior to delivery. Any substitution of equipment models requires prior written approval from the Client.

3. DELIVERY AND LOGISTICS

3.1 Delivery Schedule:

- 10 June 2024: Equipment load-in begins at 08:00 at Bayfront Event Grounds
- 11 June 2024: System installation and rigging complete by 18:00
- 12 June 2024: System tuning and alignment, 10:00–18:00
- 13 June 2024: Full technical rehearsal with artists, 14:00–22:00
- 14–16 June 2024: Festival operational days
- 17 June 2024: Load-out commences 08:00, completion by 18:00

3.2 The Vendor shall provide a delivery manifest and equipment list to the Client's site coordinator no later than 5 June 2024.

3.3 All equipment shall be transported in appropriate flight cases with clear labelling. The Vendor is responsible for all costs associated with transport, insurance, and customs clearance (if applicable).

4. PAYMENT TERMS

4.1 Total contract value: SGD 148,500.00 (excluding GST).

4.2 Payment schedule:

- 20% deposit (SGD 29,700.00) upon contract execution
- 40% (SGD 59,400.00) upon delivery of equipment to site on 10 June 2024
- 40% (SGD 59,400.00) within 30 days of successful completion of services and submission of final invoice

4.3 All invoices shall be submitted in Singapore dollars. GST shall be applied at the prevailing rate.

4.4 Late payment: The Client shall pay interest at 1.5% per month on any amount overdue beyond 30 days from invoice date.

5. VENDOR OBLIGATIONS

5.1 The Vendor shall ensure that all equipment meets the specifications set out in Schedule A and operates in accordance with manufacturer specifications throughout the festival.

5.2 The Vendor shall provide a minimum of four (4) qualified technical staff on site during the festival operational days, comprising at least one (1) system engineer, two (2) audio technicians, and one (1) RF coordinator. Staff shall be present from 08:00 to 23:00 daily during the festival period, or such other times as reasonably required by the Client for technical rehearsals and load-out.

5.3 The Vendor shall maintain a spare parts and backup equipment inventory on site at all times during the festival operational days. The minimum backup inventory shall include, but not be limited to:

- 1 x console (matching the FOH console model)
- 2 x wireless handheld transmitters
- 1 x wireless bodypack transmitter
- 2 x microphone capsules (dynamic and condenser)
- 1 x amplifier (matching the installed model)
- 100 m of 12-pair audio snake
- Assorted connectors, adaptors, and XLR cables (minimum 50 units)

5.4 The Vendor shall provide 24-hour technical support via telephone and email from the date of equipment delivery until completion of load-out. Response time for critical issues shall be within 30 minutes during operational hours and within 2 hours outside operational hours.

6. MAINTENANCE AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE

6.1 Routine maintenance: The Vendor shall perform daily system checks prior to gates opening on each operational day. Checks shall include console health, signal flow verification, wireless frequency scans, and amplifier status. A written log of these checks shall be submitted to the Client's site coordinator by 10:00 each day.

6.2 Emergency response: In the event of equipment failure during the festival operational days, the Vendor shall:

- (a) Deploy a qualified technician to the affected location within 15 minutes of notification
- (b) Attempt to restore service using backup equipment within 30 minutes
- (c) If service cannot be restored within 60 minutes, escalate to the Vendor's senior engineer
- (d) Provide a written incident report to the Client within 24 hours of the incident

6.3 Force majeure: Neither party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform its obligations under this Contract if such delay or failure arises from any cause beyond the reasonable control of that party, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, fire, flood, lightning, storm, earthquake, epidemic, pandemic, or any other natural or man-made disaster. The affected party shall notify the other party in writing within 48 hours of the occurrence of such event and shall use reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effects of the force majeure event.

7. LIABILITY AND INSURANCE

7.1 The Vendor shall maintain, at its own cost, the following insurance policies for the duration of this Contract:

- (a) Public liability insurance with a limit of not less than SGD 2,000,000 per occurrence
- (b) Employer's liability insurance as required by Singapore law
- (c) All-risk insurance on all equipment owned by the Vendor and used in connection with this Contract
- (d) Work injury compensation insurance as required under the Work Injury Compensation Act (Cap. 354)

7.2 The Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance to the Client upon request. The Client shall be named as an additional insured on the public liability policy.

7.3 Liability cap: The total aggregate liability of the Vendor under this Contract, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), or otherwise, shall not exceed the total contract value stated in Clause 4.1. Nothing in this Clause shall limit either party's liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, or death or personal injury caused by negligence.

7.4 The Vendor shall indemnify and hold harmless the Client against all claims, damages, losses, and expenses arising out of the Vendor's negligence, breach of this Contract, or infringement of any third-party intellectual property rights in connection with the equipment or services provided under this Contract.
